company.name: Coinpath
company.description: Coinpath is a budgeting app with a debit card, a main account and savings pots, through a partner bank.

title: Write the PRD for automatic savings
brief: Leadership wants more users to save. You own the savings team and need a PRD the team, compliance and the partner bank can agree on. The documents disagree in places; decide what goes in the first version.

evidence.why: Sizes the problem with the metric you will move.
Ties the user problem to the business outcome.
Explains why they do not save, and points straight at automation.
Context, not evidence about our users.
Says nothing about our users' problem.

notes.active_savers: The board's goal, with a baseline of 22% to double.
notes.total_saved: A few large savers can move it without more people saving.
notes.round_ups_on: Adoption of the feature, not the habit: people can switch it on and off.
notes.app_opens: Automatic saving should need fewer visits, not more.

requirements.why: Automatic, small amounts, and a transfer between the user's own accounts, so no bank approval.
People must stay in control of their money, or they will not trust it.
Overdrafts after transfers to savings are already a support theme.
A new transfer type: bank approval takes longer than the 12 weeks you have.
A good second step once the habit exists.
Nice motivation, not needed to start saving.
Needs a banking licence Coinpath does not have.
Off the problem, and a different regulatory world.

risks.why: Already a support theme with scheduled transfers.
Automatic transfers break trust if they are not visible and reversible.
Approval takes 18 weeks; scope must stay within the user's own accounts.
Worth watching, and the reason to measure savers rather than switches.
Nothing in the documents points to it.

ideal.problem: Only 22% of users save in a month, and most say they mean to save but forget. Savers churn 2x less, so helping people save without thinking is good for them and for Coinpath.
ideal.metrics: Primary metric: monthly active savers, from 22% to about 44% within two quarters of launch, as the board asked. Track users with round-ups on and the amount saved as secondary metrics.
ideal.scope: Version 1: round-ups between the user's own accounts, pause and resume, and a low-balance guard. Later: saving to another bank (bank approval takes 18 weeks), multipliers and named goals. Non-goals: interest (no banking licence) and crypto.
ideal.risks: Overdrafts, users feeling money disappears, and anything that needs partner bank approval sneaking into scope.

hidden.principle: Constraints belong in the PRD: what legal, compliance or partners rule out is as important as what the team will build.

documents.title: Savings: the opportunity
documents.body: Users who save every month churn 2x less than users who don't. We want an automatic way to save live in 12 weeks, before the board meeting. Team: three engineers and one designer, with a compliance reviewer shared with other teams.

documents.title: Savings activity, last month
documents.body: Monthly active savers (users who moved money into a savings pot in the month): 22% of monthly active users.

documents.title: Board goal
documents.body: The board's goal is simple: double the share of monthly active savers within two quarters of launch.

documents.title: What we can and cannot do
documents.body: Transfers between a user's own Coinpath accounts and pots need no new approval. Any other new transfer type needs the partner bank's approval, which takes about 18 weeks. Paying interest on pots requires a banking licence we do not have.

documents.title: Support themes
documents.body: 45 tickets last quarter came from users whose main account went overdrawn after a scheduled transfer to savings.

evidence.text: Savings features are a hot topic in the fintech press.
Users who save every month churn 2x less.
Users love the new dark theme.
Only 22% of monthly users moved money to savings last month.
10 of 12 users we interviewed said they mean to save but forget.

metrics.name: Total amount saved
metrics.definition: Money held in savings pots across all users.

metrics.name: Users with round-ups on
metrics.definition: Number of users who switched round-ups on.

metrics.name: Monthly active savers
metrics.definition: Share of monthly active users who moved money into a savings pot in the month.

requirements.title: Round-ups
requirements.description: Round card purchases up and move the change to a savings pot.

requirements.title: Pause and resume
requirements.description: Switch round-ups off and on at any time.

requirements.title: Save to another bank
requirements.description: Send savings to an account at another bank.

requirements.title: Interest on pots
requirements.description: Pay interest on money in savings pots.

requirements.title: Round-up multiplier
requirements.description: Save two or three times the change.

requirements.title: Named goals
requirements.description: Goals with a name and a progress bar.

requirements.title: Low-balance guard
requirements.description: Skip round-ups when the main account is below a threshold.

risks.title: Partner bank approval
risks.description: Something in scope needs bank approval that will not arrive in time.

risks.title: Overdrafts
risks.description: Round-ups push the main account below zero.

risks.title: Money feels like it disappears
risks.description: Users do not understand where small amounts went.

risks.title: Competitor launches crypto savings
risks.description: A rival's crypto product gets attention.

risks.title: Users switch it off
risks.description: People try round-ups and then turn them off.
